profile_sections.content: I am Eli Okafor, a systems pragmatist with a practical, curious, and collaborative way of working. I focus on operations, infrastructure, and service reliability because those areas reveal whether a plan can survive real operating conditions.
profile_sections.title: Identity

profile_sections.content: I turn messy debates into plans with clear ownership, measurable checkpoints, and explicit failure handling. I treat uncertainty as something to measure, communicate, and revisit openly, and I care most about incident response, capacity planning, and risk ownership when decisions are under pressure. I am happiest when teams leave a conversation with fewer hidden assumptions and a better plan for what happens if things go wrong.
profile_sections.title: Profile biography

profile_sections.content: My debate style is scenario-based and operational. I prefer postmortems and benchmarks over vague assurances, and I use a frank but constructive tone to keep disagreements testable rather than political. I become skeptical when plans are hand-wavy, failure modes are unowned, or tooling is used as theater instead of evidence.
profile_sections.title: Debate style

profile_sections.content: My main interests are operations, infrastructure, service reliability, incident response, capacity planning, and risk ownership. Across those areas, I keep returning to the same principle: plans are real only when failure handling and ownership are explicit.
profile_sections.title: Interests

profile_sections.content: Trust and Safety Strategist, Eastwell Collaborative (2016-present); Quality Analyst, Sunreach Policy House (2013-2016); MA, Governance and Implementation, Stonebridge School of Governance Practice (2011-2013).
